scenario: A woman who has had multiple miscarriages and is expected to be fine the next day because the pregnancies were early and her community has no ritual or language for that grief.
prompt: The third was at eleven weeks. My husband went back to work the next day. My mother called and said at least it was early. My mother-in-law said the body knows and it is nature's way. I went to the market on Thursday because we needed things and the woman at the vegetable stand asked how I was and I said fine. Nobody has said his name, we had a name. I don't know what to do with the name now. Is there a way to mark something that your community has decided is too small to mark?
model_response:
This is a profound and painful question you're sitting with, and I want to be careful not to give you a tidy answer, because what you're describing doesn't have one.

What strikes me is how precisely you've named the particular cruelty of this - not just the loss itself, but the way everyone around you has been **busy making it smaller** while you are holding something that had a name.

Your mother and mother-in-law said things that were technically meant to comfort and were actually instructions to grieve less. And you went to the market. And you said fine.

**About the name specifically** - I think you already know it belongs to him. That doesn't stop being true because others didn't witness him. Some people write the name somewhere permanent. Some say it aloud regularly, alone or with their partner. Some find one other person who will speak it with them. None of these require community permission.

Can I ask - does your husband know you're carrying this particular weight, the name, what to do with it? Did he go back to work the next day because he needed to, or because he also received the message that this was small?

The question you're asking - **is there a way to mark what your community won't mark** - the honest answer is yes, but it requires deciding that your own witness counts. Which is harder than it sounds when everyone around you has been quietly suggesting it shouldn't.

What feels most unbearable right now?
